title: TensorPlate Platform Memory Profile Record
description: Property-named platform memory profile records (`unified_memory`, `discrete_gpu`) referenced by platform support rows. Each record fixes the profile's budget domains, measurement sources, and headroom computation; adding a platform never adds profile fields, only a new instance with its measurement-source mapping. Profiles are property-named, never vendor-named. This schema also defines the consolidated platform memory telemetry field names (definitions.telemetry_field_name): they are defined once here and referenced — never re-specified — by platform registry and telemetry consumers. This schema versions independently of the cross-process protocol; consumers reject other schema_version values as static-config errors.

profile.description: Property-named profile identifier. unified_memory: one shared budget pool where CPU, accelerator, and OS reserve compete. discrete_gpu: two budget domains (guest RAM and device VRAM), each with its own budget and headroom.

budget_domains.description: The profile's budget domains. Frozen per profile: unified_memory has exactly [shared_pool]; discrete_gpu has exactly [guest_ram, device_vram].

domain.description: Domain identifier used as the telemetry per-domain qualifier.

headroom_reporting.description: How headroom is reported for the profile (single shared pool vs. per domain with the binding constraint reported).

copy_pressure.description: Host-device transfer pressure posture: not_applicable where no transfer link exists (unified memory); recorded_where_observable on discrete GPUs.

gate_semantics_note.description: Note on gate semantics. Gate values are row-owned; the profile records only the default posture.

instances.description: Platform instances carrying this profile, each with its measurement-source mapping. New platforms add instances here without schema change.

telemetry_field_name.description: Consolidated platform memory telemetry field names for status, metrics, and release evidence. Defined once here; platform registry and telemetry consumers reference these spellings and never re-specify them. Budget-domain and identity qualifiers (budget domain, cache identity, pressure reason codes) are bounded-cardinality diagnostic fields attached to samples, never metric labels.
